title: Identify the goal
text: We need to find values of $$\frac{5\pi}{3}+2\pi{k}$$ that fall between $$0$$ and $$4\pi.$$ Since the interval is positive, we test $$k=0$$ and positive integers.

title: Check $$k=1$$
text: When $$k=1, $$ $$\theta=\frac{5\pi}{3}+2\pi=\frac{5\pi}{3}+\frac{6\pi}{3}=\frac{11\pi}{3}.$$ This is less than $$4\pi$$ (which is $$\frac{12\pi}{3}$$ ), so it is safely in the interval.

title: Check $$k=2$$
text: When $$k=2, $$ $$\theta=\frac{5\pi}{3}+4\pi=\frac{17\pi}{3}.$$ This is greater than $$4\pi, $$ so it falls outside our boundary.

title: Compile the list
text: The only angles that fall inside the interval are $$\frac{5\pi}{3}$$ and $$\frac{11\pi}{3}.$$
